original_question: Characterize the growth rates of the Markov factors M_n(K), where M_n(K) is the operator norm of differentiation on holomorphic polynomials of degree at most n with the uniform norm on an infinite compact set K, that determine the boundary of the 'zone of uncertainty' for the extension property. Here the extension property means the existence of a continuous linear extension operator from the Whitney function space E(K) to the space of infinitely differentiable functions on R^d.
target_in_paper: Section 2, Problem 4 ("Characterize the growth rates of the Markov factors that define the boundaries of the zone of uncertainty for the extension property.")
correct_elements: Your draft correctly identifies the exact topic of the paper's Problem 4: the asymptotic growth of the Markov factors M_n(K), the existence of a nontrivial 'zone of uncertainty,' and the extension property understood as the existence of a continuous linear extension operator from the Whitney space E(K) to C^\infty(R^d). It also correctly imports the nearby definition of M_n(K) as the operator norm of differentiation on holomorphic polynomials with the uniform norm on K.
missing_details: The exact target in the paper is an open problem labeled Problem 4 in Section 2, not a conjecture or theorem.
The nearby definition is stated for a fixed n in N and an infinite compact set K; this hypothesis on K should be made explicit.
The paper's notation P_n should be spelled out as the space of holomorphic polynomials of degree at most n.
The asymptotic variable is n -> infinity; the draft should say explicitly that the growth rates are asymptotic growth rates of the sequence (M_n(K))_{n>=1}.

The surrounding context defines the 'zone of uncertainty' only indirectly: there exist compact sets K_1 with EP and K_2 without EP such that M_n(K_1) grows essentially faster than M_n(K_2) as n -> infinity, so growth of M_n(K) alone does not determine EP there.
The paper speaks of the 'boundaries' of the zone of uncertainty (plural), not a single boundary.

The paper does not formalize a specific asymptotic preorder in the statement itself; the phrase 'grows essentially faster' appears only in the surrounding discussion, so a refined stand-alone question should avoid pretending that a sharper comparison notion is already fixed in the paper.

EP is invoked in the real setting K \subset R^d, whereas the nearby Markov-factor definition is given for an infinite compact set K; a stand-alone version should keep both parts of that ambient setting visible.
refined_question: Let K be an infinite compact set, let P_n be the space of holomorphic polynomials of degree at most n endowed with the uniform norm on K, and let M_n(K) denote the operator norm of differentiation on P_n. For compact sets K \subset R^d, say that K has the extension property (EP) if there exists a continuous linear extension operator E(K) -> C^\infty(R^d). Given that there exist compact sets K_1 with EP and K_2 without EP such that M_n(K_1) grows essentially faster than M_n(K_2) as n -> infinity, so that the asymptotic growth of M_n(K) alone does not determine EP in a nonempty zone of uncertainty, characterize the asymptotic growth rates of the Markov factors that define the lower and upper boundaries of this zone of uncertainty for EP.
justification: The draft is clearly aiming at Problem 4 in Section 2 of arXiv:1612.00862. The paper first recalls the definition of the Markov factors M_n(K), then states Pleśniak's implication from the Markov property to the extension property, then explains why there is a nonempty 'zone of uncertainty' by exhibiting the qualitative comparison between a set K_1 with EP and a set K_2 without EP, and finally formulates the open problem as Problem 4. Because this paper is a short open-problems note, the nearest official formulation is Problem 4 itself; there is no sharper equivalent theorem/proposition in the paper for this item.
